# The Grids guide does not say what a commit into a sorted column does

## Context

Leaf of #18762 (public proof). Measured at user level on `examples/grid/cellEditing` (Playwright e2e rig, dev@0e3fb712ff), header clicks and keys only.

## The Problem

| Step | Firstname column, top to bottom | Header |
|---|---|---|
| boot | Tobias · Rich · Nils · Gerard · Jozef · Bastian | — |
| click the Firstname header | Bastian · Gerard · Jozef · Nils · Rich · Tobias | `neo-sort-asc` |
| edit the first row to `Zzz`, Enter | **Zzz** · Gerard · Jozef · Nils · Rich · Tobias | `neo-sort-asc` |
| click the header again | Zzz · Tobias · Rich · Nils · Jozef · Gerard | `neo-sort-desc` |
| and again | Gerard · Jozef · Nils · Rich · Tobias · Zzz | `neo-sort-asc` |

A commit into the sorted column moves nothing: the row stays where the user edited it, and the order is restored by the next sort. The same holds for a filter (measured on the pooled fixture: a committed value that no longer matches the active filter stays visible; Enter and Tab stay clean). Neither the guide nor any arm says so — a reader cannot tell a contract from an accident, and a store change that re-sorts on a record change would break Tab's walk with no arm noticing.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/data/Store.mjs#onRecordChange` (`:1330`) fires `recordChange` and nothing else; `collection.Base#autoSort` sorts "when adding / inserting" and when the sorters change (`:170`, `:256`).
- `CellEditing#getAdjacentEditableCell` already documents the premise from its side: "A logical target — record and `dataField` — so a commit that re-sorts the store cannot move it."

## The Decision This Ticket Records

The row stays put. An edit that teleports its row out from under the user — mid Tab-walk, with the next cell's editor opening somewhere else — is the worse default for a grid that is being edited, and the next sort or filter change restores the order. The alternative (re-sort and re-filter when an edit ends) is a store-wide behaviour change with its own consumers; it is out of scope here and needs its own ticket if wanted.

## The Fix

- `learn/guides/datahandling/Grids.md`, "What Scrolling Does to an Edit": one passage — a commit into the sorted column moves no row; sorters apply when THEY change. The filter half stays out of the guide: it was measured on the pooled fixture, and the public example offers no filter an arm could drive, so the guide would carry a claim without an arm.
- One arm in `test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingExample.spec.mjs`: sort by the header, commit a value that belongs at the other end, the row keeps its place and Tab's next cell is in the same row; the next header click sorts it away.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guide states that a commit into the sorted column moves no row, and when the order is restored.
- [ ] An arm on the public example pins it: after the commit the edited row keeps its position, and the next header click re-sorts it.
- [ ] The claim maps to the arm (the guide's claim → arm discipline).

## Out of Scope

- Re-sorting or re-filtering when an edit ends.
- The header's sort indicator over data an edit has unsorted.
